safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly state the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the headache is still ongoing during the consultation affects assessment of acuity, response to self-care, and safety-netting (e.g., worsening/persistent symptoms). Omission may lead to an incomplete clinical picture and suboptimal follow-up advice.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of neck stiffness (denial or presence) in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting absence of neck stiffness is important in headache evaluation because it helps risk-stratify for meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage and supports safe outpatient management. If not recorded, downstream clinicians may assume it was not assessed and may alter triage or workup.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of fever in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever status is a key associated symptom for infectious or inflammatory causes of headache; explicit denial can reduce concern for meningitis or systemic infection. Omission can drive unnecessary escalation or, conversely, obscure that appropriate screening occurred.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient currently has some sensitivity to bright lights (photophobia).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention photophobia/sensitivity to bright light.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Photophobia is clinically meaningful in a new/worse headache because it can support migraine but also raises concern for meningitis and other serious etiologies when paired with neck pain. Omitting a positive red-flag-associated symptom could contribute to under-triage or inadequate safety-netting.
